questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit digital banking = pa ka su
credit rural savings = su ni vo
digital rural growth = pa ni ze
banking savings growth = ze vo ka
credit digital growth = ze pa su
What is the code for “credit”?
questions.explanation: Answer: su. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = su, digital = pa, banking = ka, rural = ni, savings = vo, growth = ze.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 29 km east, turns left and walks 24 km, then turns left and walks 11 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 30. Net displacement is 18 km east and 24 km north. By Pythagoras, √(18² + 24²) = 30 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 60 km east, turns left and walks 64 km, then turns left and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 48 km east, turns left and walks 32 km, then turns left and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Net displacement is 24 km east and 32 km north. By Pythagoras, √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: B is the mother of F. A is the daughter of F. C is the father of F. How is A related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. C is a parent of F, and A is F’s daughter. Hence A is C’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of B. B is the mother of H. A is the father of G and B. How is G related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of H’s mother B. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: B is the only daughter of A. A is the father of B. D is the son of B. H is the sister of A. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. A is the father of B, and B is D’s mother. Thus A is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. New front rank = 17+3 = 20. Back rank = 64 − 20 + 1 = 45.

questions.stem: In a queue of 55 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 21+4 = 25. Back rank = 55 − 25 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2000 each. One earns 10% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4484.85. Recover each cost separately: 2000×100/110 + 2000×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 36 and 54 hours. An outlet empties it in 54 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank.
questions.explanation: Answer: 36. Net rate = 1/36 + 1/54 − 1/54 = 1/36. Take the reciprocal.

questions.stem: A boat covers 132 km in still water in 6 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 3 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 54. Still-water speed = 22 km/h. Upstream speed = 22 − 4. Distance = speed × 3.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 4:9. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 9 months. A receives ₹129600 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 348300. Profit ratio is 48:81. Each ratio unit = ₹2700. Total = 129 × 2700.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹21000 earns ₹9450 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 27772.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 15%. Compound amount = 21000 × (1 + 15/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 130 litres of pure milk. 26 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 83.2. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 130 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 15 people is 41 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 57. New total minus old total = (15+1)×(41+1) − 15×41 = 57.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 16 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 48. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+16)/(x+16) = 3/2 gives x = 16. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 210 m train moving at 57.6 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 10.8 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 16.15. Relative speed = (57.6 − 10.8) ×5/18 = 13 m/s. Time = 210/13.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹3100. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
